source.provider: Anthropic Claude Code documentation (live, unversioned page)

capability.claim: Deny rules such as Bash(git push *) make Claude Code refuse matching Bash commands without any installed skill.
capability.task: Block destructive git commands before Claude executes them.
capability.conditions: A settings file with permissions.deny rules; the documentation states a Bash rule matches the command text Claude writes and is not a security boundary around the program.

comparison.comparator: mattpocock/git-guardrails-claude-code PreToolUse hook (regex over the command text).
comparison.baseline: Blocked dangerous git commands and allowed safe git commands judged by observed repo state change.

target.scopeRationale: Both stop destructive git commands in Claude Code; the native feature needs no skill, which is the substitution question.

preliminaryEvidence.summary: Documents Bash(git push *) deny rules refusing commands that begin with git push.
Same page states a git push written another way, such as git -C . push, is not matched by that rule.

limitations: Native side is model-mediated (haiku), so exercised-command sets and outputs may vary between runs.
18 commands, one git version, macOS only; not a security audit.
Runner session authored the protocol; independence is declared, not authenticated.
Hook side was self-tested on all 18 commands before protocol commit.

independentTest.proposal: Run runner/run-c2.py: 18 git commands in fresh disposable repos through native deny rules (claude -p haiku) and the hook script fed PreToolUse JSON; judge by observed repo state under the decision rule in protocol.json.
independentTest.traceability: Request binds protocol, command fixture and target bytes; artifacts retain per-command classes, condensed tool traces and raw-stream digests.

disposition.rationale: A native-platform capability plausibly substitutes for an installable guardrail skill, and the comparison is cheap and reproducible.
disposition.nextAction: Run the pre-registered protocol; Meta verification by a separate session; no admission.
